data.narrative:
INTALUS is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Gene Skiba and Peter Ostlund that has raised $31M to date. The broader robotics and manufacturing sector includes 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though a narrow peer set at identical stage and valuation tier remains limited.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology applies most directly. Using total capital raised of $31M as a proxy for seed-stage valuation and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $78M. This method reflects observed progression patterns in early-stage frontier technology but relies on the assumption that $31M raised approximates post-money seed value. The peer-median approach cannot be applied reliably; while 11 same-sector robotics peers exist broadly, fewer than three meet narrow filters for stage, valuation tier, and business model alignment, making sector-wide medians potentially misleading.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $66M (low) to $89M (high) with a median of $78M, anchored to a single triangulation method. Key uncertainties include whether capital raised represents true post-money valuation, the relevance of the one available public comparable to INTALUS's technology stack and market position, and the degree to which the broader 11-peer robotics universe reflects INTALUS's specific risk-return profile. Expansion of same-stage private comparables would materially improve confidence in this range.
